Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked very strong. As we move toward finalizing the MSA + Order Form, procurement and our legal team have a couple of open items around third-party IP claims.

Specifically: Neptune prefers a defend-and-control approach for third-party infringement claims for outputs generated by the vendor (your side). Our initial ask is that Redwood accept defend-and-control for claims that arise from (a) model code, or (b) outputs where Redwood’s proprietary model or prompt templates are the proximate cause.

We understand you have standard carveouts and caps; to be productive, can you share a short proposal showing:
- where Redwood would accept defend-and-control vs. reimburse-only;
- typical notice/cooperation timelines you require; and
- any insurance/escrow/indemnity caps you would need.

Attached is a redacted sample third-party claim notice we received in another deal for your reference. Happy to set a 30m sync if useful — procurement is aiming to finish MSA redlines by next week.

Attachments: sample-claim-notice.pdf (PDF, 312 KB)

Sarah — thanks for the clear note and the sample claim. I copied Kimberly (legal) and Ben (sales) so we can move this quickly. High level response below; Kimberly will follow up with specific redlines.

Short answer: Redwood is open to a defend-and-control pathway for a bounded set of third-party IP claims, but we need to preserve certain carveouts (open-source, customer-supplied data/instructions, and misuse). We also typically pair defend-control with:
- a cooperation clause (reasonable assistance + privileged counsel coordination),
- a notice window (30 days from receipt of claim to trigger), and
- an overall liability cap tied to the Order Form value or a multiple (we can propose hard numbers).

To keep momentum, we prepared a one-page internal proposal that outlines a compromise bridge (defend for Redwood-controlled models/production prompts; reimburse for customer-modified models or outputs derived from customer data). Attaching that now.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly to send redline of the relevant MSA sections (indemnity, notice, cooperation, carveouts).
2) Ben and I to align commercial cap and insurance threshold with procurement.
3) If needed, 30m call Thursday to finalize.

Attachment: proposed-bridge-summary.docx (DOCX, 28 KB)

Thanks — we should be able to land this quickly if we agree on the carveouts and timeline.

Subject: Proposed redlines — defend vs. reimburse bridge

Sarah / Neptune team,

Thanks for sending the sample claim. I reviewed Logan’s bridge proposal and sketched redlines that reflect Redwood’s operational constraints. Key points:

1) Scope trigger (where Redwood will defend):
- Redwood will accept defend-and-control for third-party claims solely to the extent the claim arises from Redwood’s proprietary model weights, training artifacts, or Redwood-authored prompt sequences provided as part of the managed product.

2) Carveouts (we will NOT defend):
- claims arising from Customer-provided prompts, data, fine-tuned customer models, or Customer’s modifications;
- claims that result from Customer misuse (breach of AUP) or deployment outside supported configurations.

3) Notice & cooperation:
- Customer must provide notice "promptly" and in any event within 30 calendar days of becoming aware;
- Customer must not settle or admit liability without Redwood’s consent (consent not to be unreasonably withheld) and must provide reasonable cooperation (document production, witness statements).

4) Allocation & control mechanics:
- Redwood retains primary control of defense, including selection of counsel subject to mutual approval for conflicts;
- If Redwood elects to defend, Customer may participate at its own expense. Where Redwood declines to defend, Redwood may reimburse reasonable damages and costs as set out in the Order Form.

5) Cap & insurance:
- We propose a cap equal to the greater of (i) 2x annual contract value for the 12-month term, or (ii) $2M per claim, with a general aggregate tied to the Order Form.
- We can include an insurance covenant (commercially reasonable CGL + tech E&O) to back this.

6) Evidence handling & privilege:
- Redwood will coordinate privilege preservation; evidence custody processes to be agreed in the SOP appendix.

I attached a redline PDF with inline edits and suggested language for the Order Form to make the cap/trigger explicit. If this looks acceptable we can convert to tracked redline for your counsel.

Attachments: MSA-redline-diff.pdf (PDF, 64 KB)

I’m available for a short call next week to walk through the language.
